mainTopic: Preparations for מילה on שבת and יום טוב, food-preparation limits on יום טוב (mustard, cheese), and אביי's mother's baby-care advice, including when to postpone a מילה.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a list of baby remedies, then returns to the משנה about a מוהל who did not grind cumin before שבת. A ברייתא teaches that grinding כמון and mixing יין ושמן for a מילה are forbidden on שבת but allowed on יום טוב. אביי challenges this, since רבי מאיר permits mixing wine and oil for a sick person on שבת. A story shows that רבי מאיר was only strict on himself and never retracted his view. The גמרא answers that a מילה needs the mixture beaten, which is forbidden on שבת, but mixing without beating is allowed. Next, אביי and רב יוסף discuss preparing mustard and curdling cheese on יום טוב. Straining mustard looks like בורר, and a wooden coal may not be used to sweeten it. Cheese may not be curdled on יום טוב because it could have been made beforehand without losing quality. Finally, אביי passes on his foster mother's advice on bandaging a מילה and caring for newborns. The amud ends with the rule that a red or pale baby's מילה is postponed, proven by two stories of רבי נתן.

steps.title: A remedy for a child with skin sores
steps.stepSummary: The last item in a list of baby remedies: a child with sores should be washed often in beet water.
steps.simpleTranslation: A child with sores: what is his remedy? Let him be washed a lot in water in which beets were boiled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a list of folk remedies for babies by naming one more problem, sores (חספניתא), and its cure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line belongs to the medical discussion that came just before it, not to the new topic. Once it ends, the גמרא goes back to the laws of מילה on שבת.

phrases.english: A child with sores.
phrases.notes: The case being treated.

phrases.english: What is his remedy?
Let him wash a lot in beet water.
phrases.notes: Water in which beets were boiled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list of medical remedies from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child with sores is treated by washing him often in beet water.

steps.title: Some preparations for a מילה are allowed on יום טוב but not on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about not grinding cumin before שבת and brings a ברייתא: grinding כמון and mixing יין ושמן for a מילה are allowed on יום טוב but not on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he did not grind it before שבת.' The Rabbis taught: Some things may not be done for a מילה on שבת, but may be done for it on יום טוב. One grinds cumin for it, and one mixes wine and oil for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and brings a ברייתא listing preparations for a מילה that are forbidden on שבת but allowed on יום טוב. This is the base text for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two examples: grinding כמון and mixing יין ושמן to put on the wound. Both are forbidden on שבת but allowed on יום טוב. This raises the question of what makes יום טוב more lenient here.

keyTerms.meaning: Cumin, used as a healing powder on the מילה wound
Wine and oil, mixed as a salve

steps.confusionAlert: The ברית מילה itself is permitted on שבת. This ברייתא is only about the preparations around it (grinding, mixing), which do not override שבת.

phrases.english: If he did not grind it before Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Things that one may not do for a circumcision on Shabbat
one may do for it on a Festival.
One grinds cumin for it,
and one mixes wine and oil for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין לַמִּילָה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the remedies and returns to the משנה's laws of מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grinding כמון and mixing יין ושמן for a מילה are forbidden on שבת but permitted on יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי asks: if cumin is allowed because it is fit for food, why not wine and oil on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that if cumin is allowed on יום טוב because it is fit for cooking, then wine and oil should be allowed on שבת, since they are fit for a sick person.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: What makes cumin different on יום טוב? It is fit for a pot. But wine and oil are also fit, on שבת, for a sick person!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the ברייתא's line between שבת and יום טוב. He suggests why cumin is allowed on יום טוב, then shows that the same reason would allow wine and oil even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cumin is allowed on יום טוב because people grind spices for cooking that day, so it is a normal permitted act. By the same logic, mixing wine and oil is normally permitted on שבת for a sick person, so it should be permitted for a מילה too. That would contradict the ברייתא, which forbids it on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks for the distinguishing reason)
Since it is fit or usable

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
What is different about cumin on a Festival?
Because it is fit for a cooking pot.
phrases.notes: It is a cooking spice, so grinding it on יום טוב is ordinary food preparation.

phrases.english: Wine and oil are also fit
phrases.notes: The same reasoning applied.

phrases.english: on Shabbat, for a sick person,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's distinction between שבת and יום טוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that mixing יין ושמן for a מילה is forbidden on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'fit for normal use' permits cumin on יום טוב, then 'fit for a sick person' should permit wine and oil on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that wine and oil may be mixed for a sick person on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ברייתא: the first view forbids mixing wine and oil for a sick person on שבת, but רבי מאיר permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One may not mix wine and oil for a sick person on שבת. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said in the name of רבי מאיר: One may even mix wine and oil.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up his claim that wine and oil are 'fit for a sick person on שבת' with a ברייתא that records רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא records a מחלוקת. The first view forbids, and רבי מאיר permits. אביי's challenge depends on רבי מאיר's lenient view, so the next steps show that רבי מאיר never retracted it, even though he was personally strict.

phrases.english: As it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין טוֹרְפִין יַיִן וָשֶׁמֶן לַחוֹלֶה בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: One may not mix wine and oil for a sick person on Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
One may even mix wine and oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין טוֹרְפִין יַיִן וָשֶׁמֶן לַחוֹלֶה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for אביי's claim in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That wine and oil count as 'fit for a sick person on שבת'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי מאיר permits mixing wine and oil for a sick person on שבת.

steps.title: רבי מאיר refuses the treatment when he is sick
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר tells how רבי מאיר, sick on שבת, would not let his students mix wine and oil for him. The students protested.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: Once רבי מאיר had stomach pain, and we wanted to mix wine and oil for him, but he did not let us. We said to him: Will your own words be cancelled in your lifetime?!
steps.whatsHappening: A story is told in which רבי מאיר seems to act against his own lenient ruling. It sets up the question of whether he took back his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר refused, perhaps he no longer held his lenient view, which would weaken אביי's challenge. The students ask exactly this: is he cancelling his own teaching?

keyTerms.meaning: Had pain in his stomach or intestines

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת חָשׁ רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּמֵעָיו,
phrases.english: Once Rabbi Meir had pain in his intestines,
and we wanted to mix wine and oil for him
and he did not let us.
We said to him:
Will your words be cancelled in your lifetime?!
phrases.notes: You yourself ruled leniently!

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּעַם אַחַת חָשׁ רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּמֵעָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story about how רבי מאיר acted on the ruling cited in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר personally refused wine and oil on שבת despite his lenient view.

steps.title: רבי מאיר explains: I would not act against my colleagues
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that he still holds his view, but he never felt bold enough to act against his colleagues' opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to us: Even though I say one thing and my colleagues say another, all my life I never felt bold enough to go against my colleagues' words.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר answers his students. He has not retracted his ruling. He is simply choosing to be careful for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He separates what he teaches (it is permitted) from how he personally behaves (he respects the other view). So the story does not cancel his lenient ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: My heart was bold enough (I dared)

phrases.english: He said to us:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר כָּךְ
phrases.english: Even though I say this
and my colleagues say that,
in all my days my heart never dared
to go against the words of my colleagues.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר כָּךְ וַחֲבֵירַי אוֹמְרִים כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' protest from Step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבי מאיר retract his lenient ruling?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. He keeps his view but personally avoids acting against his colleagues.

steps.title: It was a personal stringency; for everyone it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי מאיר was only strict on himself. For everyone else, mixing wine and oil for a sick person on שבת is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was the one being strict on himself, but for everyone else it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the story: רבי מאיר's ruling stands, and his refusal was only a private stringency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms the basis of אביי's challenge: wine and oil really are 'fit for a sick person on שבת'. So the question still stands: why does the ברייתא forbid mixing them for a מילה on שבת? The next step answers this.
steps.whatToRemember: Grinding כמון and mixing יין ושמן for a מילה are allowed on יום טוב but not on שבת. אביי asks why wine and oil are forbidden on שבת when רבי מאיר permits them for a sick person, and רבי מאיר's personal stringency does not change that ruling for others.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key principle: a sage's personal stringency is separate from his halachic ruling. It also keeps אביי's question standing, so the גמרא must answer it in the next step.

phrases.english: He was the one being strict on himself,
but for everyone it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the halachic lesson from רבי מאיר's answer in Step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Per רבי מאיר, mixing wine and oil for a sick person on שבת is permitted for all. This strengthens אביי's challenge to the ברייתא.

steps.title: For a sick person the mixture is not beaten, but for מילה it must be
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers אביי: for a sick person the wine and oil do not need to be beaten, but for a מילה they must be beaten, and beating is what is forbidden on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: There (for a sick person), it does not need to be beaten. Here (for מילה), it needs to be beaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's challenge from Step 3: if wine and oil may be mixed on שבת for a sick person, why does the ברייתא forbid mixing them for a מילה on שבת? The answer is that the two cases need different preparation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine and oil for a sick person only need to be poured together, so no real work is done. A מילה wound dressing needs the mixture beaten, and that beating is forbidden on שבת but allowed on יום טוב. So the ברייתא's line between שבת and יום טוב stands, and it does not contradict רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: there (the case of the sick person)

phrases.english: There, it does not need beating,
phrases.notes: The case of the sick person: simple mixing is enough.

phrases.english: here, it needs beating.
phrases.notes: The case of מילה: the mixture must be beaten into a paste.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא בָּעֵי לִיכָּא הָכָא בָּעֵי לִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge (Step 3), now strengthened by Step 7, by distinguishing the sick person's mixture from the beaten mixture needed for מילה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since mixing wine and oil is allowed on שבת for a sick person, preparing it for a מילה should also be allowed on שבת, contrary to the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: For מילה the mixture must be beaten, which is forbidden on שבת but allowed on יום טוב. That is why the ברייתא permits it only on יום טוב.

steps.title: Why not mix for מילה without beating?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: for מילה too, let him mix the wine and oil but simply not beat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, let him make the mixture and not beat it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If only the beating is the problem, he could mix the two liquids and skip the beating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The distinction in Step 8 shows only that beating is forbidden on שבת. So for a מילה on שבת, why not mix the wine and oil without beating, just as is done for a sick person?

phrases.english: Here too, let him prepare it and not beat it!
phrases.notes: Mixing alone should be allowed, just as it is for a sick person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on Step 8: if only beating is the problem, the mixture could be made for a מילה on שבת without beating.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of Step 8 that wine and oil cannot be prepared for a מילה on שבת at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only beating is forbidden, mixing without beating should be allowed for מילה as well.

steps.title: That is exactly what the משנה means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's phrase 'each by itself' means exactly this: he may mix them but not beat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what it teaches: 'He puts this by itself and that by itself.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the challenge and explains that the משנה's words were meant this way all along.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This by itself and that by itself' does not mean the two liquids may never touch. It means each is used as it is, without being beaten together into a paste. So mixing is allowed for מילה too, and only beating is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Mixing wine and oil is allowed on שבת both for a sick person and for מילה. What is forbidden is beating them together into a paste.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'this by itself and that by itself' as 'never put them together.' According to the גמרא, it means 'don't beat them together.'

phrases.english: That is what it teaches:
He puts this by itself
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: and that by itself.
phrases.notes: He means each one is mixed in, but not beaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of Step 9 and rereads the משנה's wording to match it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Each by itself' means the liquids may not be mixed at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Each by itself' means they are mixed but not beaten.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids straining mustard and sweetening it with a coal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may not strain mustard in its strainer, and one may not sweeten it with a hot coal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not strain mustard in its strainer, and one may not sweeten it with a coal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a ברייתא with two rules about preparing mustard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straining mustard separates the coarse parts from the fine parts, which is a concern of בורר. Sweetening means dropping a hot coal into the mustard to soften its sharpness, and that puts the coal out (כיבוי). Both rules are discussed in the steps that follow.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְסַנְּנִין אֶת הַחַרְדָּל בִּמְסַנֶּנֶת שֶׁלּוֹ,
phrases.english: One may not strain mustard in its strainer,
phrases.notes: The problem here is selecting (בורר).

phrases.english: and one may not sweeten it with a coal.
phrases.notes: Placing a hot coal in it puts the coal out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵין מְסַנְּנִין אֶת הַחַרְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic about preparing mustard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Straining mustard in its strainer and sweetening it with a coal are forbidden.

steps.title: אביי compares this to putting an egg in a mustard strainer
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף how this differs from the משנה that allows putting an egg into a mustard strainer.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: What is the difference between this and what we learned in a משנה: 'One may put an egg into a mustard strainer'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the first rule of the ברייתא by pointing to a משנה that seems to allow straining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring an egg through a mustard strainer into the mustard, to improve its appearance, also uses a strainer. If that is allowed, why is straining mustard forbidden?

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
What is different from that which we learned:
One may place an egg in a mustard strainer?
phrases.notes: A משנה permitting this on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first rule of the ברייתא in Step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה allows using the same strainer for an egg, so straining mustard should be allowed too.

steps.title: Only the mustard looks like selecting
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that straining an egg does not look like בורר, but straining mustard does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, it does not look like selecting. Here, it looks like selecting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains the difference between the egg and the mustard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the egg, the whole egg is food, so passing it through the strainer does not look like separating good from bad. Straining mustard separates the fine part from the coarse waste, which looks like real בורר. So only the mustard is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: selecting, one of the forbidden מלאכות

steps.whatToRemember: An act that separates good food from waste looks like בורר and is forbidden. An act that does not look like separating can be allowed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There, it does not look like selecting,
phrases.notes: "There" means the egg.

phrases.english: here, it looks like selecting.
phrases.notes: "Here" means the mustard.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא מִיחְזֵי כְּבוֹרֵר הָכָא מִיחְזֵי כְּבוֹרֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Straining an egg and straining mustard are the same act.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only straining mustard looks like בורר, so only it is forbidden.

steps.title: Another ברייתא allows sweetening with a coal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ban on sweetening mustard with a coal and challenges it from a ברייתא that allows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one may not sweeten it with a coal.' But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: 'One may sweeten it with a coal'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the second rule of the ברייתא and shows that another ברייתא says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ברייתות contradict each other directly. One forbids sweetening mustard with a coal and the other allows it, so the גמרא needs a way to reconcile them.

phrases.english: And one may not sweeten it with a coal.
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא from Step 11.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
One may sweeten it with a coal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the second rule of Step 11 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ban on sweetening mustard with a coal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different ברייתא explicitly allows it.

steps.title: Metal coal versus wooden coal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: a metal coal is allowed and a wooden coal is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: here it means a coal of metal, and there it means a coal of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of coal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting out a glowing metal coal is not כיבוי מדאורייתא, so the ברייתא that permits sweetening is talking about metal. Putting out a wooden coal is real כיבוי, so the ברייתא that forbids it is talking about wood.
steps.whatToRemember: Sweetening mustard with a hot coal: a metal coal is allowed, and a wooden coal is forbidden because putting it out is כיבוי.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, with a metal coal,
phrases.notes: Permitted: putting out metal is not כיבוי מדאורייתא.

phrases.english: there, with a wooden coal.
phrases.notes: Forbidden: putting out wood is כיבוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן בְּגַחֶלֶת שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות disagree about the same act.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permitting ברייתא means a metal coal, and the forbidding ברייתא means a wooden coal.

steps.title: Why is mustard different from meat roasted on coals?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף why a wooden coal is forbidden for mustard when meat may be roasted on coals, even though the dripping juices put out some of the coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: How is this different from meat placed on coals?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the rule from Step 15 that a wooden coal may not be used to sweeten mustard. He points to roasting meat on coals, which is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wooden coal is forbidden because putting it into the mustard puts out the fire (כיבוי). But when meat roasts on coals, its juices drip down and also put out some of the coals, and that is allowed. So why is one case forbidden and the other allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (a formula asking why two similar cases get different rulings)

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
What is different from meat on coals!
phrases.notes: The meat's juices drip and put out the coals, yet roasting is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ban on the wooden coal stated in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that sweetening mustard with a wooden coal is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Meat on coals also causes coals to be put out, yet it is allowed. So putting out a coal should not make the mustard case forbidden either.

steps.title: Meat has no other option, mustard does
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that meat could not be roasted before יום טוב, but mustard could have been sweetened beforehand.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There it is not possible; here it is possible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains the difference between the two cases. Meat has no other way to be roasted, but mustard has an alternative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat must be roasted on יום טוב itself, because it is best eaten fresh and hot, so dripping onto the coals is allowed. Mustard can be sweetened the day before without losing quality, so there is no need to put out a coal on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Possible, meaning there is another way to do it

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the 'is there another option?' reasoning that רב יוסף uses again in Step 21 about cheese.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There (with meat), it is not possible (to do it beforehand);
here (with mustard), it is possible (to do it beforehand).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: whether there is another way to do it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since meat on coals is allowed, any similar case of putting out coals should be allowed too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Putting out coals on יום טוב is tolerated only when the food could not have been prepared beforehand. Mustard could have been sweetened the day before, so the wooden coal is forbidden.

steps.title: May one curdle cheese on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether one may curdle milk into cheese on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: What is the law about curdling cheese (on יום טוב)?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new but related question: may cheese be made on יום טוב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, food preparation (אוכל נפש) is generally allowed. אביי wants to know whether making cheese counts as allowed food preparation.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law? (a formula for asking a question)

steps.confusionAlert: This question is about יום טוב, not שבת. On יום טוב many food-preparation acts are allowed, which is why the question is even asked.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
What is the law about curdling (cheese, on a Festival)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question from the same teacher-student pair, using the same kind of reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether curdling cheese is allowed on יום טוב.

steps.title: Curdling cheese is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that curdling cheese on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a short, direct answer: it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not give a reason yet. The reason comes out only after אביי challenges him in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Curdling cheese on יום טוב is forbidden.

steps.title: Why is cheese different from kneading dough?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the answer: kneading dough is allowed on יום טוב, so why not curdling cheese?
steps.simpleTranslation: How is it different from kneading?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's ruling by comparing it to kneading dough, which is allowed on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kneading is also a food-preparation act, and it is allowed on יום טוב. If kneading is allowed, why should curdling cheese, which is also food preparation, be forbidden?

phrases.english: What is different from kneading?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ban on curdling cheese on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Kneading is a similar food-preparation act and is allowed, so curdling should be allowed too.

steps.title: Bread must be fresh, cheese can be made earlier
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers with the same principle as before: bread cannot be prepared before יום טוב without losing quality, but cheese can.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There it is not possible; here it is possible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף uses the same short formula he used about meat. This time it means bread could not have been made earlier, but cheese could have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Day-old bread is not as good as fresh bread, so it cannot be baked before יום טוב, and kneading on יום טוב is allowed. Cheese can be made before יום טוב without getting worse, so there is no need to make it on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible (here: it could not have been done before יום טוב)

steps.confusionAlert: The words are the same as in Step 17, and so is the meaning: 'possible' means 'possible to do before יום טוב without losing quality.'

phrases.english: He said to him:
There (with bread), it is not possible (to prepare beforehand);
here (with cheese), it is possible (to prepare beforehand).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20, using the same formula as Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: whether it could have been done before יום טוב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All food-preparation acts like kneading are allowed on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: An act is allowed only if doing it before יום טוב would lower the food's quality. Cheese does not lose quality, so it must be made beforehand.

steps.title: The scholars of נהרדעא praise fresh cheese
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the answer: the scholars of נהרדעא said one-day-old cheese is excellent, which suggests fresh cheese is best.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the scholars of נהרדעא say: One-day-old cheese is excellent!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's claim that cheese can be made ahead of time without losing quality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one-day-old cheese is the best, then cheese is like bread: freshness matters. So making cheese on יום טוב should be allowed, just like kneading.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely... (introduces a challenge from a known statement)
The scholars of the city נהרדעא

phrases.english: But didn't the Sages of Neharde'a say:
One-day-old cheese is excellent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual claim in Step 21 that cheese does not lose quality when made in advance.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that cheese can be prepared before יום טוב without losing quality.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נהרדעא's statement implies that fresh cheese is the best, so cheese should be treated like bread.

steps.title: Even fresh cheese is good, but aged is better
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rereads the statement of נהרדעא: they meant that even one-day-old cheese is good, not that it is the best.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they are saying: That even one-day-old cheese is excellent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains that אביי misread the statement of נהרדעא. It does not praise fresh cheese as the best.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' changes everything. Fresh cheese is acceptable, but older cheese is better. So there is no reason to make cheese on יום טוב, and the ban stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what they mean (introduces a reinterpretation)

steps.whatToRemember: Curdling cheese on יום טוב is forbidden. Kneading is allowed only because bread is best fresh, while cheese only improves with age. A food act on יום טוב is justified when it truly could not have been done before.

phrases.english: This is what they are saying:
that even one-day-old cheese is excellent (but older is better).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22 by reinterpreting the statement of נהרדעא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fresh cheese is the best, so cheese is like bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fresh cheese is merely acceptable, and aged cheese is better, so there is no need to make it on יום טוב.

steps.title: Back to the משנה about the pouch for the מילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה that one may not make a חלוק (pouch) for the מילה wound on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not make a pouch for it, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה to discuss its next detail. This line sets up אביי's practical teachings in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that on שבת one may not make a new חלוק, a small pouch-like bandage placed over the ברית מילה. The גמרא quotes it now to add practical guidance about how such a pouch should be used.

keyTerms.meaning: A pouch or small cap placed over the מילה wound
Etc. (the rest of the quote continues)

phrases.english: One may not make a pouch for it, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the cheese discussion and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת one may not make a pouch for the מילה wound from scratch.

steps.title: אביי's mother: put the pouch on with its threads away from the wound
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports his mother's advice: put the pouch on the baby with the frayed side facing up, so a thread does not stick to the wound and cause permanent damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My mother told me: That pouch of a baby, turn it with its side upward, lest a thread from it stick, and it lead to a severed urethra.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי passes on practical medical advice from his mother about how to place the pouch on a newly circumcised baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pouch has loose threads along its edges. If those threads touch the fresh wound, they can stick and cause serious injury. So the threaded side must be turned away from the wound.

keyTerms.meaning: Mother (here, the nursemaid who raised אביי)
A person whose urethra was severed, a serious permanent injury

steps.confusionAlert: When אביי says 'my mother,' he means the nursemaid who raised him. His birth mother died when he was born, and he quotes this woman many times.

phrases.english: Abaye said: My mother told me:
That pouch of a baby,
let one turn it with its side upward,
phrases.notes: So the frayed threads are not near the wound.

phrases.english: lest a thread from it stick (to the wound),
and he come to be one with a severed urethra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds practical detail to the משנה's חלוק quoted in Step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Place the pouch with its threaded side facing up, away from the wound, to prevent injury.

steps.title: אביי's mother made a half-size pouch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that אביי's mother made a pouch that covered only half, so its threads would not touch the wound.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי's mother would make a pouch for half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how אביי's mother actually made these pouches, as an example of the advice in Step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her pouch covered only half of the area. This kept the threaded edges away from the wound, carrying out the same safety concern in practice.

phrases.english: Abaye's mother
would make a pouch (covering) half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the advice of Step 25 was carried out in real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pouch covering only half keeps its threads away from the wound.

steps.title: What to do if the baby has no pouch
steps.stepSummary: אביי teaches: if there is no pouch, take a worn cloth with a hem, put the hem underneath, and fold the cloth over, so no loose threads touch the wound.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A baby who has no pouch: let one bring a worn-out cloth that has a hem, wrap the hem underneath, and fold it over on top.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a backup solution for when no proper pouch is available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hem is a finished edge with no loose threads. Placing the hem against the wound and folding the rest of the cloth over it protects the baby from stray threads, just as the pouch advice did.

keyTerms.meaning: A hem, a finished edge of cloth

steps.whatToRemember: With a newly circumcised baby, the key concern is keeping loose threads away from the wound. Use a pouch turned with its threads up, a half-size pouch, or a hemmed cloth with the hem against the wound.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
That baby who does not have a pouch —
let one bring a worn-out cloth that has a hem,
and wrap the hem underneath (against the wound),
and fold it over on top.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative for when the pouch described in Steps 24 and 25 is not available.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without a pouch, use a hemmed worn cloth with the hem underneath and fold the cloth over, so no threads touch the wound.

steps.title: Opening a baby's blocked exit
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes his mother: if a baby's anus is covered by skin, rub it with oil and hold it to the light. Where the skin looks see-through, cut it crosswise with a barley grain, not with metal.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My mother told me: If a baby's exit cannot be found, rub the spot with oil and hold it up to the daylight. Where it looks see-through, tear it open crosswise with a barley grain. Do not use a metal tool, because metal causes swelling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list of אביי's practical baby advice from his mother. This one is about a baby born with skin covering the anus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil and the light make the thin spot visible, so the cut is made in the right place. The barley grain is preferred because a metal tool causes infection and swelling.
steps.confusionAlert: The word אֵם here does not mean אביי's birth mother. אביי's mother died when he was born, so this is the woman who raised him (his nurse). That is why some translations say 'my nurse.'

phrases.english: And Abaye said: My mother told me:
phrases.notes: Refers to the woman who raised him.

phrases.english: A baby whose exit (anus) cannot be found,
let one rub it with oil
and stand it facing the daylight,
and where it looks see-through
let one tear it with a barley grain, widthwise and lengthwise.
But with a metal tool, no,
because it causes swelling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of אביי's mother's baby-care teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Locate the hidden opening with oil and light, then cut it crosswise with a barley grain, not metal.

steps.title: A baby who will not nurse
steps.stepSummary: A baby who won't suck has a cold mouth. Hold a cup of hot coals near his mouth to warm it, and he will nurse.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My mother told me: A baby who does not suck does so because his mouth is cold. What is the fix? Bring a cup of coals and hold it near his mouth. His mouth warms up and he sucks.
steps.whatsHappening: Another piece of advice from אביי's mother. She gives the reason a baby refuses to nurse and how to fix it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The advice gives a cause (a cold mouth) and then a remedy that matches it (warmth from coals). The cup simply brings heat close to the baby's mouth.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: My mother told me:
A baby who does not suck,
it is because his mouth is cold.
What is his remedy?
Let them bring a cup of coals,
and hold it near his mouth,
so his mouth warms up and he sucks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Warm a non-nursing baby's mouth with nearby coals.

steps.title: A baby who does not urinate
steps.stepSummary: Shake the baby in a sieve and he will urinate.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My mother told me: A baby who does not urinate should be shaken in a sieve, and he will urinate.
steps.whatsHappening: A short remedy from אביי's mother for a baby who is not passing urine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gentle shaking motion stimulates the baby's body, and that helps him urinate.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: My mother told me:
A baby who does not urinate
let one shake him in a sieve, and he will urinate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shake a non-urinating baby in a sieve.

steps.title: A baby who is not breathing
steps.stepSummary: Bring the mother's placenta and rub it on the baby, and he will breathe.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My mother told me: A baby who is not breathing: bring his mother's placenta and rub it on him, and he will breathe.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי's mother gives a remedy for a newborn who is not breathing. It uses the mother's placenta.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The placenta was the baby's source of life in the womb. The remedy uses it to revive the baby's breathing.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: My mother told me:
A baby who does not breathe
let them bring his mother's placenta
and rub it on him, and he will breathe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rub the mother's placenta on a non-breathing baby.

steps.title: A baby who is too small or too large
steps.stepSummary: Rub the placenta on a small baby from its narrow end to its wide end. For a baby who is too big, rub from the wide end to the narrow end.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My mother told me: A baby who is too small: bring his mother's placenta and rub it on him from the narrow end to the wide end. If he is too big, rub from the wide end to the narrow end.
steps.whatsHappening: This remedy also uses the placenta. Here it is meant to fix a baby's size in either direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The direction of rubbing matches the goal. Narrow-to-wide is for growing a small baby. Wide-to-narrow is for reducing an oversized one.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: My mother told me:
A baby who is too small,
let them bring his mother's placenta,
and rub it on him
from the narrow end to the wide end.
And if he is too big, from the wide end to the narrow end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues using the placenta, now for size problems.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rubbing direction depends on whether the baby is too small or too large.

steps.title: Delay מילה for a red or pale baby
steps.stepSummary: A red baby's blood has not yet been absorbed, so wait until it is and then do the מילה. A pale baby's blood has not yet entered his body, so wait until it does and then do the מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My mother told me: A baby who is red, because his blood has not yet been absorbed into him, should be left until his blood is absorbed, and then they should circumcise him. A baby who is pale, because his blood has not yet entered him, should be left until his blood enters him, and then they should circumcise him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last of אביי's mother's teachings here, and it connects back to מילה. She says when the מילה must be postponed for the baby's health.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two opposite problems. In a red baby the blood is still near the surface and not settled in. In a pale baby there is too little blood. In both cases, doing the מילה now is dangerous, so it is pushed off until the baby is healthy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical halachic source: a baby's health comes before doing the מילה on time. The next steps prove it with real cases.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: My mother told me:
A baby who is red,
because his blood has not yet been absorbed into him,

phrases.aramaic: לִיתָּרְחוּ לֵיהּ עַד דְּמִיבְּלַע בֵּיהּ דְּמֵיהּ,
phrases.english: let them wait for him until his blood is absorbed into him,
and then circumcise him.

phrases.aramaic: דְּיָרוֹק, דְּאַכַּתִּי לָא נְפַל בֵּיהּ דְּמֵיהּ
phrases.english: One who is pale, because his blood has not yet entered him,
let them wait until his blood enters him,
and then circumcise him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item in the list, returning to the topic of מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Postpone מילה for a red or pale baby until his blood settles.

steps.title: רבי נתן and the red baby
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: in the coastal cities, a woman had lost two sons after מילה. רבי נתן saw that her third son was red, told her to wait, and the baby lived.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי נתן said: Once I went to the coastal cities. A woman came to me who had circumcised her first son and he died, and her second and he died. She brought the third to me. I saw he was red. I told her: Wait until his blood is absorbed into him. She waited until it was absorbed, then circumcised him, and he lived. They named him 'נתן הבבלי' after me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the red-baby rule from the step before. This story covers the red case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word דְּתַנְיָא tells us a source is coming to back up what was just said. The first two babies died after their מילה. When the third was given time, he survived, which shows the danger and the remedy are real.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Natan said:
Once I went to the coastal cities,
and a woman came before me
who had circumcised her first son and he died,
the second, and he died,
the third, she brought him before me.
I saw that he was red.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתִּי לָהּ: הַמְתִּינִי לוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּבָּלַע בּוֹ דָּמוֹ,
phrases.english: I said to her: Wait until his blood is absorbed into him.

phrases.aramaic: הִמְתִּינָה לוֹ עַד שֶׁנִּבְלַע בּוֹ דָּמוֹ,
phrases.english: She waited until his blood was absorbed into him,
then circumcised him, and he lived.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ קוֹרִין אוֹתוֹ ״נָתָן הַבַּבְלִי״ עַל שְׁמִי.
phrases.english: And they would call him 'Natan the Babylonian' after my name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the red-baby half of אביי's rule.
steps.raayaObject: A red baby's מילה should be delayed until his blood is absorbed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי נתן: the story in the coastal cities

steps.title: רבי נתן and the pale baby
steps.stepSummary: In קפוטקיא, another woman had lost two sons after מילה. Her third son was pale and showed no blood of the covenant. רבי נתן told her to wait, and the baby lived.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time I went to the land of קפוטקיא. A woman came to me who had circumcised her first son and he died, and her second and he died. She brought the third to me. I saw he was pale. I looked at him closely and saw no blood of the covenant in him. I told her: Wait until his blood enters him. She waited, then circumcised him, and he lived. They named him 'נתן הבבלי' after me.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא continues with a second story. This one supports the pale-baby half of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This baby had the opposite problem: too little blood, so רבי נתן could not see the דַּם בְּרִית. Waiting worked again. Together with the first story, it proves both parts of אביי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: the blood of the covenant (blood that flows at מילה)

steps.whatToRemember: Danger to a baby's life comes before doing the מילה on time. A red baby or a pale baby waits until his blood settles, as אביי's mother taught and as רבי נתן's two stories prove.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּב פַּעַם אַחַת הָלַכְתִּי לִמְדִינַת קַפּוֹטְקְיָא,
phrases.english: Another time I went to the land of Cappadocia,
and a woman came before me
who had circumcised her first son and he died,
the second, and he died,
the third, she brought him before me.
I saw that he was pale.

phrases.aramaic: הֵצַצְתִּי בּוֹ וְלֹא רָאִיתִי בּוֹ דַּם בְּרִית.
phrases.english: I looked at him closely and did not see in him the blood of the covenant.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתִּי לָהּ: הַמְתִּינִי לוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּפּוֹל בּוֹ דָּמוֹ,
phrases.english: I said to her: Wait until his blood enters him.
She waited, then circumcised him, and he lived.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ קוֹרִין שְׁמוֹ ״נָתָן הַבַּבְלִי״ עַל שְׁמִי.
phrases.english: And they would call his name 'Natan the Babylonian' after my name.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּב פַּעַם אַחַת הָלַכְתִּי לִמְדִינַת קַפּוֹטְקְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second story in the same ברייתא, proving the pale-baby half.
steps.raayaObject: A pale baby's מילה should be delayed until his blood enters him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי נתן: the story in קפוטקיא
